title: Context and memory in an agent

items.stem: A makerspace assistant run takes three model calls. The system prompt and tool descriptions take 1,000 tokens and the student's question 100 tokens. On call 1 the model requests a tool (a 50-token request); the tool result is 600 tokens. On call 2 the model requests another tool (50 tokens); that result is 200 tokens. On call 3 the model writes the final answer. The program re-sends the full history on every call. How many input tokens are sent in total across the three calls?

A student finished 3D printer training last week. Today they open a new chat with your assistant and ask, "Can I book the printer?" What is the most dependable way for the assistant to know the training is done?

options.text: The model recalls it from last week's chat because it has talked to them
A tool reads the student's training record from storage outside the model
The model has a large window, so last week's chat still fits inside it
The system prompt is rewritten by the model each night to include all students

items.stem: Your team proposes putting all 40 machine manuals, about 2 million tokens in total, into the context on every request, since some current models have large windows. Which is the strongest objection?

options.text: Every token is billed on every call, and answer quality can fall as context grows
A model cannot read text that was not part of its training data
A tool result is never allowed to be larger than the user's question
Large windows are only available when the conversation is a single turn

items.stem: In one sentence, name one thing a program can do when a long agent run is nearly out of context space, so that the run can continue.

A student's training status sits in the makerspace's database. In one sentence, why is it better for the assistant to fetch one student's record with a tool when needed than to paste every student's record into the system prompt?
